name: Bangladesh
summary: Bangladesh Bank licenses and supervises scheduled banks under the Bank-Company Act 1991 (amended 2023) and issues binding circulars and guidelines. The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) enforces the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012 and the Anti-Terrorism Act 2009. BFIU Circular 26 and the MLP Rules 2019 expressly require AML/CFT/CPF training for all officers, and BFIU guidelines add annual board awareness. Bangladesh Bank requires security awareness on joining and every year (ICT Security Guideline 4.0), cybersecurity training under the 2026 framework, a 14-week foundation course for new officers (2026), and role-based compliance training (2026 internal control guidelines). BSEC regulates listed banks. A 2026 Personal Data Protection Act and Labour Act amendments on harassment also apply.

regulators.name: Bangladesh Bank
regulators.role: Central bank and prudential regulator of scheduled banks under the Bank-Company Act 1991; issues binding circulars and guidelines on governance, ICT security, cybersecurity, internal control, customer service and training.

regulators.name: Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit
regulators.role: Financial intelligence unit and AML/CFT/CPF supervisor of reporting organisations under the MLPA 2012 and ATA 2009; receives STRs and CTRs and issues AML circulars and guidance.

regulators.name: Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.role: Capital market regulator; applies listing and corporate governance conditions to listed banks and supervises capital market intermediaries.

programs.title: Bangladesh | MLPA 2012 and BFIU Circular 26 AML Training for Bank Officers
programs.why: The MLP Rules 2019 require every reporting organisation's compliance programme to provide for staff training, and BFIU Circular 26 directs each bank to give all officers suitable, target-oriented AML/CFT/CPF training with refreshers at intervals and to keep training records. BFIU's risk management guidelines add that every employee needs at least a day-long basic course with assessment, refreshed regularly, and that staff should be trained before being placed on a desk.

references.title: Money Laundering Prevention Rules, 2019
references.issuer: Ministry of Finance (Financial Institutions Division), published by BFIU
references.note: A reporting organisation's own compliance programme must provide for naming a compliance officer, screening when hiring, training officers, and independent audit.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.provision: Paragraph 11.2 (training of bank officers) and paragraph 12(2) (training records)
references.note: Banks must arrange suitable ML/TF/PF training for all officers, meaning basic and role-related, level- and department-specific training plus periodic refreshers; CAMLCO, deputy CAMLCO and other relevant officers need training or professional certification; training records must be kept.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Every employee should complete at least a day-long basic AML/CFT course with an evaluation, followed by regular refreshers, and job-specific training for trade, international, credit and transaction roles; staff should have the relevant training before taking up a desk.

references.title: Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 (Act No. 5 of 2012, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Sets the core duties of reporting organisations: keep accurate customer identification records, retain account and transaction records for at least five years after closure, supply them to BFIU, and report suspicious transactions promptly on their own initiative.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Combating Terrorist Financing under the Anti-Terrorism Act 2009
programs.why: The Anti-Terrorism Act 2009 obliges reporting agencies to take care to prevent and detect terrorist-financing transactions and to report suspicions without delay, and makes the board responsible for issuing staff instructions. BFIU Circular 26 is issued under both the MLPA and the ATA and its training paragraph expressly covers terrorist financing, so the AML/CFT training programme must teach TF typologies, listed persons and reporting.

references.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 2009 (Act No. 16 of 2009, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Bangladesh Bank (through BFIU) may direct reporting agencies, monitor them and arrange training for their staff; each reporting agency must take due care to prevent and detect TF transactions and report suspicious ones to Bangladesh Bank without delay, and its board must approve staff instructions and ensure compliance.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: The required officer training covers money laundering, terrorist financing and financing of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, with refreshers at intervals.

references.title: Guidance Notes for Prevention of Terrorist Financing and Financing of Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction
references.note: BFIU's guidance on TF and PF expects reporting organisations to arrange training and awareness for staff alongside screening and freezing procedures.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Countering Proliferation Financing (BFIU Circular 26 and CTPF Guidance)
audience: Trade finance and international operations staff
programs.why: Bangladesh treats proliferation financing as part of the same compliance regime: BFIU Circular 26 requires banks to screen against UN Security Council lists on WMD proliferation, freeze matches and inform BFIU, and its training paragraph expressly includes financing of proliferation. BFIU's CTPF guidance asks banks to build training and awareness around these duties.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Banks must screen customers and transactions against UNSC lists on terrorism and proliferation, freeze matches immediately and report to BFIU by the next working day; officer training must cover PF as well as ML and TF.

references.title: Guidance Notes for Prevention of Terrorist Financing and Financing of Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction
references.note: Expects reporting organisations to maintain screening, handle false positives, review policies against sanctions regimes and arrange staff training and awareness on TF and PF.

references.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 2009 (Act No. 16 of 2009, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Empowers Bangladesh Bank to direct reporting agencies to take preventive steps against financing of terrorism and of weapons of mass destruction and to arrange staff training.

programs.title: Bangladesh | KYC under BFIU Circular 26 and the 2026 e-KYC Guidelines
audience: Account opening and customer service officers
programs.why: Circular 26 sets the customer acceptance policy and KYC steps for every account, and Bangladesh Bank's March 2026 e-KYC guidelines govern remote onboarding. BFIU's risk management guidelines require due diligence and transaction-monitoring training for the employees who deal with customers, on top of basic AML training for everyone.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Requires a customer acceptance policy and KYC procedures for identifying and verifying customers before establishing relationships.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Besides basic and refresher training, banks must give job-specific CDD and transaction-monitoring training to staff who handle customer transactions, and UNSCR screening training to account-opening and customer-relations staff.

references.title: Guidelines on Electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC), March 2026
references.note: Bangladesh Bank's 2026 rules for remote, electronic onboarding of bank customers, built on the MLP Rules 2019 and BFIU instructions.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Customer Due Diligence (MLPA s.25 and BFIU Circular 26)
programs.why: The MLPA requires accurate and complete customer identification records, and Circular 26 details CDD, simplified due diligence and walk-in customer rules. BFIU expects customer-facing and transaction-processing staff to receive specific CDD training in addition to basic AML training.

references.title: Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 (Act No. 5 of 2012, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Reporting organisations must keep accurate and full customer identification information and keep account and transaction records for at least five years after an account closes.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Sets KYC, customer due diligence, simplified due diligence and other CDD requirements for scheduled banks.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Requires CDD and ongoing-monitoring training for employees who conduct customer transactions.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Enhanced Due Diligence for High-Risk Customers (BFIU Circular 26)
programs.why: Circular 26 requires enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers, PEPs, influential persons and heads of international organisations. No separate EDD course is prescribed; staff who apply EDD must understand the triggers and measures, which the general role-based AML training must cover.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Requires EDD for higher-risk customers and specific measures for PEPs, influential persons and senior officials of international organisations, including approval by the bank's Chief Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer (CAMLCO) and source-of-funds checks (BFIU Circular 26 paras 3.10 and 3.13).

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Role-based training must equip staff for the CDD tasks they perform.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Ongoing Due Diligence and Transaction Monitoring by Branch Staff
programs.why: Banks must keep customer profiles current and monitor transactions against them. BFIU's guidelines expressly require customer due diligence and ongoing transaction monitoring training for employees who process customer transactions, and BAMLCOs must cover transaction monitoring in quarterly branch AML meetings.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Requires transaction monitoring and quarterly branch AML meetings, led by the BAMLCO, on KYC, transaction monitoring, STR identification, sanctions, self-assessment, record keeping and training.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Requires CDD and ongoing-monitoring training for staff who conduct customer transactions.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Beneficial Ownership Identification (BFIU Guidelines)
programs.why: Banks must identify and verify the natural persons behind legal persons and arrangements. BFIU has issued beneficial ownership guidelines, but no separate training requirement; competence is expected through the general AML training programme.

references.title: Guidelines for Beneficial Owner
references.note: Sets out how to identify and verify the natural persons who ultimately own or control a customer, including legal persons and arrangements.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Customer due diligence includes identifying the beneficial owner of accounts.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Politically Exposed Persons and Influential Persons (BFIU)
programs.why: Circular 26 sets specific measures for foreign PEPs, domestic influential persons and heads of international organisations, supported by BFIU's PEP guidance notes. Staff need to know how to identify and handle these customers, but no stand-alone PEP training is prescribed.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Requires risk-based identification of PEPs and influential persons, CAMLCO approval (BFIU Circular 26 para 3.10), source-of-wealth checks and enhanced monitoring.

references.title: Guidance Notes on Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) for all Reporting Organizations
references.note: Explains how reporting organisations identify domestic and foreign PEPs and influential persons, obtain senior approval and monitor such relationships.

programs.title: Bangladesh | UNSCR and Domestic Sanctions Screening
audience: Account opening and customer relations staff
programs.why: Banks must screen customers and transactions against UN Security Council lists and the Government's domestic list. BFIU's guidelines expressly require UNSCR screening training for all employees who deal with international transactions, customer relations and account opening.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Requires electronic screening against UNSC and domestic lists, regular checks for listed persons' accounts and transactions, records of false positives, and immediate freezing with a report to BFIU.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Names UNSCR screening training as job-specific training for staff dealing with international transactions, customer relations and account opening.

references.title: Guidelines on Implementation of the UN Security Council Resolutions concerning Targeted Financial Sanctions, Travel Ban and Arms Embargo
references.issuer: National Committee on Implementation of UNSC Resolutions (Ministry of Foreign Affairs), published by BFIU
references.note: Explains the legal basis and coordination arrangements for UN targeted financial sanctions in Bangladesh and BFIU's role in directing reporting agencies.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Targeted Financial Sanctions: Freezing and Reporting to BFIU
programs.why: When a listed person's account or transaction is found, the bank must freeze it at once and give BFIU full details by the next working day, following BFIU's guidance on terrorist and proliferation financing. Staff who screen and handle such cases must receive the UNSCR screening training BFIU requires.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: On identifying an account or transaction of a listed or proscribed person, the bank must freeze it immediately and report details to BFIU by the next working day.

references.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 2009 (Act No. 16 of 2009, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Gives Bangladesh Bank powers to freeze and direct reporting agencies and sets the reporting agencies' duty to prevent and report TF transactions.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Requires UNSCR screening training for staff handling international transactions, customer relations and account opening.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Suspicious Transaction Reporting to BFIU (MLPA s.25 and ATA s.16)
programs.why: Both the MLPA and the ATA require banks to report suspicious transactions or attempts to BFIU promptly and on their own initiative. BFIU requires the basic AML/CFT course for every employee to cover the STR/SAR reporting procedure, and its STR guidance describes a three-stage identify, evaluate and report process.

references.title: Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 (Act No. 5 of 2012, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: A reporting organisation must report any suspicious transaction or attempted transaction to BFIU immediately and on its own initiative.

references.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 2009 (Act No. 16 of 2009, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Reporting agencies must report suspected terrorist-financing transactions to Bangladesh Bank without delay and on their own initiative.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Sets the STR process for scheduled banks, from branch identification to submission by the AML/CFT department.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: The basic AML/CFT course for all employees must cover the STR/SAR reporting procedure.

references.title: Guidance on Reporting Suspicious Transaction Report for the Reporting Organization
references.note: Describes the identification, evaluation and reporting stages and says staff training on spotting unusual activity should be continuous.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Identifying Unusual Transactions (BFIU STR Guidance)
programs.why: Spotting unusual activity is the first stage of STR reporting. Circular 26 makes all officers' training cover the ML/TF risks of their own work, and BFIU's STR guidance says training staff to identify unusual or suspicious activity should be an ongoing activity.

references.title: Guidance on Reporting Suspicious Transaction Report for the Reporting Organization
references.note: Identification of unusual activity is the first STR stage; it should be supported by systems and by continuous staff training.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Officer training must include role-related ML/TF risk content and periodic refreshers.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Transaction Monitoring and Alert Handling
programs.why: Circular 26 requires banks to monitor transactions and BFIU issued further instructions in 2026 on enforcing transaction monitoring systems at scheduled banks. BFIU's guidelines require monitoring-specific training for the staff who perform these tasks.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Requires scheduled banks to monitor customer transactions to detect unusual and suspicious activity.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Requires CDD and ongoing-monitoring training for staff who conduct customer transactions.

references.title: BFIU Circular Letter No. 02: Instructions for the Scheduled Banks for the Enforcement of Transaction Monitoring System
references.note: Listed on BFIU's circular letter page; the published file is a scanned image, so its text could not be read automatically.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Trade-Based Money Laundering (BFIU TBML Guidelines)
audience: Trade finance and foreign exchange officers
Trade operations and LC processing staff
programs.why: Bangladesh faces significant trade-based money laundering risk. BFIU's 2019 TBML guidelines make training essential for officials at all levels in trade, require role-based training for day-to-day trade processors, make TBML a core part of the training plan and require training records. BFIU's risk management guidelines separately list TBML training for trade staff.

references.title: Guidelines for Prevention of Trade Based Money Laundering (issued with BFIU Circular No. 24)
references.note: Banks must assess TBML training needs; training is essential for trade officials at all three levels, role-based for daily trade processors, part of the core training calendar, and recorded.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Lists TBML training as job-specific training for employees dealing with foreign or domestic trade.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Correspondent Banking Due Diligence (BFIU Circular 26)
audience: Correspondent banking and financial institutions team
programs.why: Circular 26 sets due diligence conditions before and during correspondent relationships, including assessing the respondent's AML/CFT controls, senior approval and a ban on shell banks. No separate training is prescribed; staff managing these relationships need working knowledge of the rules.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Sets the information-gathering, approval and monitoring conditions for establishing and keeping correspondent banking relationships.

programs.title: Bangladesh | ML/TF Risk Assessment and the Risk-Based Approach (BFIU)
programs.why: BFIU's 2015 risk assessment guidelines require banks to assess ML/TF risks by customer, product, delivery channel and geography and expect an ML/TF risk management system that includes training programmes to build staff expertise in identifying these risks. The duty is framed as part of the risk framework rather than a stand-alone course.

references.title: Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment Guidelines for Banking Sector
references.note: Lists the components of a bank's ML/TF risk management system, including suitable training programmes for staff to build expertise in identifying ML/TF risk.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Banks need a board-approved AML/CFT policy and must assess ML/TF risks before launching new products, services or technologies.

programs.title: Bangladesh | AML Record Keeping and Cash Transaction Reporting
programs.why: The MLPA requires account and transaction records to be kept for at least five years after closure and supplied to BFIU on request. Circular 26 also requires records of training, meetings and inspections, and sets monthly cash transaction reporting. Staff handling records and CTRs need to know these rules; no separate course is prescribed.

references.title: Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 (Act No. 5 of 2012, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Keep complete customer identification data, retain account and transaction records for at least five years after closure, and supply them to BFIU when asked.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Sets cash transaction reporting and requires retention of CDD and transaction records for at least five years, plus records of AML training, meetings and inspections.

programs.title: Bangladesh | AML/CFT for Branch Staff and BAMLCOs (BFIU Circular 26)
audience: Branch Anti Money Laundering Compliance Officers (BAMLCOs)
programs.why: Each branch must have a BAMLCO who knows the laws, rules and BFIU instructions and who holds quarterly AML meetings covering KYC, monitoring, STRs, sanctions, self-assessment, records and training. Branches complete half-yearly self-assessments that check how many officers have had formal AML training. All officers must receive training and refreshers.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: Requires a BAMLCO in every branch with sound knowledge of the rules, quarterly branch AML meetings that cover training, half-yearly branch self-assessments, and training for all officers.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Staff must have relevant AML training before taking a desk and complete basic and refresher training.

programs.title: Bangladesh | AML/CFT Oversight for the Board, CEO and CAMLCO
audience: Chief Anti Money Laundering Compliance Officer (CAMLCO) and deputy
programs.why: BFIU's risk management guidelines require banks to hold an AML/CFT awareness programme for all board members at least once a year. Circular 26 requires the CEO to issue an annual statement of commitment to all staff, a senior-level Central Compliance Committee and CAMLCO, and training or professional certification for the CAMLCO, deputy CAMLCO and other relevant officers.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Banks must arrange an AML/CFT awareness programme for all board members (or the top policy committee) at least once a year.

references.title: BFIU Circular No. 26: Instructions for scheduled banks on preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing
references.note: The CEO must issue a clear annual commitment statement to all staff; banks must set up a Central Compliance Committee led by a CAMLCO; CAMLCO, deputy CAMLCO and other relevant officers must get training and/or professional certification.

references.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 2009 (Act No. 16 of 2009, as amended)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: The board, or the CEO where there is no board, must approve and issue instructions on officers' duties and ensure Bangladesh Bank's directions are followed.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Anti-Bribery, Gifts and Conflicts under the Bangladesh Bank Code of Conduct
programs.why: There is no stand-alone anti-bribery training rule for banks. Bangladesh Bank's Code of Conduct bans gifts that create obligations and requires staff to avoid conflicts of interest, and banks must disseminate it to staff. The 2026 internal control guidelines make bribery and kickbacks reportable through the whistleblower channel.

references.title: Code of Conduct for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions
references.note: Requires employees to avoid conflicts of interest, restricts acceptance of gifts and foreign awards, treats misuse of position as corruption, and makes banks responsible for disseminating the code to employees.

references.title: BRPD-2 Circular No. 03: Guidelines on Internal Control Management System in Banks (July 2026)
references.note: Lists bribery, kickbacks, corruption and fraud among the issues staff can report under the mandatory whistleblower framework.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Fraud Prevention and the Anti-Fraud Self-Assessment (Bangladesh Bank)
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's 2026 foundation training guidelines make financial fraud prevention a required topic for all newly recruited officers, and completion is a condition for confirmation in service. Under the 2026 internal control guidelines, department heads and branch managers must complete an anti-fraud internal control checklist every six months, and BFIU expects credit-fraud and ML training for credit staff.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 10: Guidelines on Foundation Training for the Newly Recruited Scheduled Bank Officials
references.note: Foundation training (at least 14 weeks) is mandatory for confirming new officers and must include financial fraud prevention among its minimum content.

references.title: BRPD-2 Circular No. 03: Guidelines on Internal Control Management System in Banks (July 2026)
references.note: Department heads and branch managers must complete the Self-Assessment Anti-Fraud Internal Control Checklist each half-year, covering internal control, general banking, credit, foreign exchange and ICT.

references.title: Money Laundering & Terrorist Financing Risk Management Guidelines (Banks)
references.note: Requires credit fraud and ML training for employees dealing with advances and credit.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Banking Laws and Regulations in Bangladesh Bank Foundation Training
audience: Newly recruited officers (management trainees, probationary and other officers)
Officers promoted without prior foundation training
programs.why: Since May 2026 every scheduled bank must run foundation training of at least 14 weeks for newly recruited officers, and completing it is required for confirmation in service. The minimum curriculum includes the Bank Company Act, foreign exchange law, the Money Loan Court Act, the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, the Negotiable Instruments Act, the MLPA and key Bangladesh Bank circulars.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 10: Guidelines on Foundation Training for the Newly Recruited Scheduled Bank Officials
references.note: Banks must treat the guidelines as a minimum standard, adopt board-approved training policies, deliver 8 weeks of theory and 6 of practice, and cover major banking laws and regulations; the directive was issued under section 45 of the Bank Company Act and took effect immediately.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Role-Based Compliance Training under the 2026 Internal Control Guidelines
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's July 2026 Guidelines on Internal Control Management System replaced the 2016 ICC guidelines. They require the compliance function, together with HR, to develop and deliver a mandatory, role-based compliance training programme based on the compliance risk assessment, and to measure and report its effectiveness. Banks must restructure to the new system by 31 December 2026.

references.title: BRPD-2 Circular No. 03: Guidelines on Internal Control Management System in Banks (July 2026)
references.note: Compliance and HR must deliver a mandatory, role-based compliance training programme built on the compliance risk assessment and report on its effectiveness; ICMS staff must also receive advanced local and foreign training. The circular repeals the 2016 ICC circulars and sets a 31 December 2026 deadline.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Corporate Governance of Bank-Companies (Bank Company Act and BRPD Circular 02/2024)
programs.why: The Bank Company Act (as amended in 2023) and BRPD Circular 02 of 2024 set board composition, independent directors, committees and board duties. The board must stress staff training and include it in the annual plan, and must adopt a code of conduct and ethics for all staff. These are governance duties rather than a prescribed course.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 02: Formation of Board and Responsibilities of Directors of a Bank-Company
references.note: Sets board formation, board responsibilities and committee rules; the board must give special importance to staff training in its annual work plan and must adopt a code of conduct and code of ethics for all staff.

references.title: Bank-Company Act, 1991 (Act No. 14 of 1991, as amended up to 2023)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Section 15 governs bank directors, including at least three independent directors and a 20-member cap; section 45 lets Bangladesh Bank issue binding directions to banks.

references.title: BRPD Circular Letter No. 14: Formation of Board and Responsibilities of Directors of a Bank-Company
references.note: Requires board and committee minutes to record discussions, dissenting views, notes of dissent and Bangladesh Bank observers' comments; other BRPD Circular 02/2024 instructions are unchanged.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Directors' Duties and Director Training (BRPD Circular 02/2024)
programs.why: BRPD Circular 02 of 2024 sets the duties of bank directors and says training on banking law, related laws and changed regulations may be arranged for directors within the country. Because the wording is permissive, director training is a competence expectation rather than a set obligation; separate annual AML awareness for the board is covered under program 26.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 02: Formation of Board and Responsibilities of Directors of a Bank-Company
references.note: Sets board duties and allows in-country training for directors on banking laws, related rules and changed banking regulations and policies.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Fit and Proper Criteria for Bank Directors (BRPD Circular 02/2024)
programs.why: A bank director must have at least 10 years of management, business or professional experience, be at least 30, have no criminal, fraud or regulatory-breach record, not be a defaulter or wilful defaulter, and avoid conflicting roles. Bangladesh Bank's prior approval is needed for appointment. These are fitness standards, not a training requirement.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 02: Formation of Board and Responsibilities of Directors of a Bank-Company
references.note: Lists eligibility and suitability criteria for directors and requires Bangladesh Bank's prior approval for appointment and reappointment.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Bangladesh Bank Code of Conduct and Ethics for Bank Staff
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's Code of Conduct requires banks to adopt it, circulate it to staff, train staff to act with integrity, and organise seminars, workshops and training to promote ethics and compliance. The 2026 foundation training guidelines also require new officers to be trained on the bank's code of conduct and on ethics and professional integrity.

references.title: Code of Conduct for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions
references.note: Banks must train staff to act with integrity, organise and sponsor seminars and workshops on ethics, integrity and compliance, formally circulate the code within 60 days, and have an ethics committee with an annual work plan.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 10: Guidelines on Foundation Training for the Newly Recruited Scheduled Bank Officials
references.note: New officers' foundation training must cover the bank's code of conduct, staff regulations and HR policy, and ethics and professional integrity.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 02: Formation of Board and Responsibilities of Directors of a Bank-Company
references.note: The board must adopt a code of conduct and code of ethics for all staff and build a compliance culture.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Whistleblower Framework (Internal Control Guidelines 2026 and PID Act 2011)
audience: All employees, including contractual and temporary staff
Head of Compliance and Audit Committee
programs.why: Every bank must run a whistleblower framework with confidential channels, anonymous reporting, protection against retaliation and a set investigation process. The Public Interest Information Disclosure Act 2011 also protects people who report public-interest wrongdoing to a competent authority. Staff must know the channels, but no specific training is prescribed.

references.title: BRPD-2 Circular No. 03: Guidelines on Internal Control Management System in Banks (July 2026)
references.note: Banks must establish a whistleblower framework for staff, directors and external parties covering fraud, bribery, policy and regulatory breaches, with confidential channels, anonymity and protection from retaliation.

references.title: Public Interest Information Disclosure (Provide Protection) Act, 2011 (Act No. 7 of 2011)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Protects people who disclose public-interest information in good faith to a competent authority, including private institutions' staff, against demotion, harassing transfer and similar reprisals.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Customer Service Standards under the Bangladesh Bank Customer Services Guidelines
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's customer service guidelines expect a board-approved branch management policy that includes customer-service-oriented staff training, a staff code of conduct, customer booklets and indicator boards, and an annual customer satisfaction survey. The Consumer Rights Protection Act 2009 does not list banking among the services it covers, so customer conduct rules come mainly from Bangladesh Bank.

references.title: Guidelines for Customer Services and Complaint Management (issued by FICSD Circular No. 01 of 13 July 2014)
references.note: Banks should adopt a branch management policy covering customer information, service counters, surprise inspections, customer-service training and suitable products, and set a code of conduct for officials.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Complaint Handling through Customer Service and Complaint Management Cells
audience: Customer service and complaint management cell staff
Zonal and head office complaint units
programs.why: Banks must run a three-tier complaint structure (head office, zonal and branch cells), resolve complaints within set times, report complaint statistics to Bangladesh Bank, and display Bangladesh Bank's 16236 hotline. The guidelines expressly require banks to train customer-service officials to improve their skill and knowledge.

references.title: Guidelines for Customer Services and Complaint Management (issued by FICSD Circular No. 01 of 13 July 2014)
references.note: Requires central, zonal and branch customer service and complaint management cells, complaint timelines and reporting to Bangladesh Bank, and training for customer-service officials.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 07: Displaying Bangladesh Bank's hotline number (16236) with the bank's own hotline
references.note: Head office, branches and sub-branches must show Bangladesh Bank's 16236 hotline next to the bank's own hotline on complaint boxes in a visible place; issued under section 45 of the Bank Company Act.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Escalating Complaints to Bangladesh Bank
programs.why: Bangladesh has no separate banking ombudsman. A customer who is not satisfied with a bank's answer can complain to Bangladesh Bank, whose advice or orders the bank must follow. Complaint staff should know this route; no training is prescribed.

references.title: Guidelines for Customer Services and Complaint Management (issued by FICSD Circular No. 01 of 13 July 2014)
references.note: Customers dissatisfied with a bank's resolution may lodge a formal complaint with Bangladesh Bank, and banks must comply with Bangladesh Bank's advice or orders on the complaint.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Customer Confidentiality and Personal Data (Code of Conduct and PDPA 2026)
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's Code of Conduct requires staff to keep customers' affairs secret, and the Personal Data Protection Act 2026 now bars disclosing personal data for any purpose other than the one it was collected for without consent. Staff must know these duties; no specific training is prescribed.

references.title: Code of Conduct for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions
references.note: Requires complete secrecy of customers' affairs and account information and protection of confidential information.

references.title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2026 (Act No. 63 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Personal data may not be disclosed beyond its collection purpose without consent; controllers and processors must take suitable technical and organisational security measures.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Information Security Awareness (Bangladesh Bank ICT Security Guideline v4.0)
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's ICT Security Guideline 4.0 requires banks to give all staff security awareness training as early as possible after they join and every year after that, to run security awareness and education for general users, to hold periodic risk and information security seminars covering all employees, and to train management on ICT security responsibilities.

references.title: Guideline on ICT Security for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions, Version 4.0 (issued by BRPD Circular No. 10 of 19 June 2023)
references.note: Security awareness training for all staff at the start of employment and annually after that; management training on ICT security and governance; general user awareness and periodic information security seminars for all employees.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Cybersecurity Awareness under the Bangladesh Bank Cybersecurity Framework 2026
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's 2026 Cybersecurity Framework, which banks must comply with by 31 December 2026, requires awareness and training programmes, including periodic training for all staff on security policies and cyber hygiene, and awareness or training for vendors. The 2026 foundation training guidelines also make data protection and cyber security a required topic for new officers.

references.title: Guidelines on Cybersecurity Framework, Version 1.0 (2026)
references.note: Banks must provide cybersecurity awareness education, periodic training for all staff on security policies and cyber hygiene, certifications for security staff, training for privileged users, executives and physical security staff, and awareness for third parties.

references.title: BRPD-2 Circular No. 02: Cybersecurity Framework, Version 1.0 (2026)
references.note: Issues the framework to banks, finance companies, MFS, PSPs and PSOs; it covers cyber governance, risk, incident management, and training and awareness, with compliance due by 31 December 2026.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 10: Guidelines on Foundation Training for the Newly Recruited Scheduled Bank Officials
references.note: Foundation training for new officers must cover data protection and cyber security.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Cyber Risk Management Roles (Cybersecurity Framework 2026)
programs.why: The Cybersecurity Framework requires regular training sessions and customised training for specific technical roles, and standard certifications for information security staff. The Cyber Security Act 2026 also lets the Government declare critical information infrastructure, which brings extra monitoring, inspection and audit.

references.title: Guidelines on Cybersecurity Framework, Version 1.0 (2026)
references.note: Calls for regular training and programmes tailored to administrators and developers, recognised certifications for information security staff, and role training for privileged users and executives.

references.title: Cyber Security Act, 2026 (Act No. 81 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Provides for declaring critical information infrastructure and for monitoring, inspecting and auditing its security.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Personal Data Protection Act 2026
programs.why: The Personal Data Protection Act 2026 (Act 63 of 2026) replaced the 2025 ordinances. It is deemed in force from 6 November 2025, except the Chief Data Officer duty and the complaint, fine and compensation sections, which start on a date to be notified after 18 months. It sets lawful bases, consent, security, retention and breach rules but no staff training duty.

references.title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2026 (Act No. 63 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Sets lawful processing and consent, security measures and breach notification to the Authority; significant controllers will need Chief Data Officers once section 23 is brought into force.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Phishing and Email Security Awareness (ICT Security Guideline v4.0)
programs.why: The ICT Security Guideline requires an email security awareness session for every new joiner within 60 days, covering phishing detection and incident reporting, and recommends a yearly refresher. Its social engineering section requires awareness training at the start of employment and annually that teaches staff to spot social engineering and resist phishing.

references.title: Guideline on ICT Security for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions, Version 4.0 (issued by BRPD Circular No. 10 of 19 June 2023)
references.note: New joiners must attend an email security awareness session within 60 days (yearly refresher recommended); all staff must get social engineering and phishing awareness on joining and annually.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Cyber Incident Response and Reporting to Bangladesh Bank
programs.why: The ICT Security Guideline requires role-based incident response training with simulated events and specific training for the CIRT. The 2026 Cybersecurity Framework requires critical cyber incidents to be reported internally and to stakeholders, including BGD e-GOV CIRT and Bangladesh Bank, within 72 hours.

references.title: Guideline on ICT Security for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions, Version 4.0 (issued by BRPD Circular No. 10 of 19 June 2023)
references.note: Incident response training must match users' roles and include simulated events; the CIRT must be trained; security events must be reported quickly through management.

references.title: Guidelines on Cybersecurity Framework, Version 1.0 (2026)
references.note: Banks need a process to report cyber incidents to the regulator, and must report critical incidents to internal and external stakeholders, including BGD-CIRT and Bangladesh Bank, within 72 hours.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Personal Data Breach Notification (PDPA 2026)
programs.why: Where a personal data breach is likely to cause significant harm, the controller must notify the data protection Authority in the form and time set by regulations. Combined with Bangladesh Bank's 72-hour cyber incident reporting rule, incident staff need to know both routes; no training is prescribed.

references.title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2026 (Act No. 63 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: A controller must notify the Authority of a personal data breach likely to cause significant harm, in the manner and time set by regulations.

references.title: Guidelines on Cybersecurity Framework, Version 1.0 (2026)
references.note: Critical cyber incidents must be reported to Bangladesh Bank and other stakeholders within 72 hours.

programs.title: Bangladesh | ICT Governance and ICT Risk Management (ICT Security Guideline v4.0)
programs.why: The ICT Security Guideline applies to banks, NBFIs, MFS providers, PSPs and PSOs. It requires professional security training and certification for IT personnel, business foundation training for ICT staff, training facilities for the IS audit team when services or technology change, and training of internal trainers.

references.title: Guideline on ICT Security for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions, Version 4.0 (issued by BRPD Circular No. 10 of 19 June 2023)
references.note: Applies the guideline to all Bangladesh Bank-regulated financial service providers and requires professional security training for IT staff, business foundation training for ICT personnel, IS audit training and train-the-trainer arrangements.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Risk Management Guidelines for Banks 2018: Risk Culture and the Annual Risk Conference
audience: Chief Risk Officer and risk management department
Branch managers and deputy branch managers
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's 2018 risk guidelines make risk management everyone's job and tell banks to build risk culture through training. They give the CRO express duties to hold a yearly risk conference for all branch managers and their deputies and to arrange risk training for risk department officials, so these roles need regular enterprise risk training.

references.title: Risk Management Guidelines for Banks, 2018 (DOS Circular No. 04)
references.note: Banks must build a risk culture through policies, communication and staff training. The Chief Risk Officer must hold an annual risk conference for all branch managers and deputies and arrange internal and external risk training for risk management department officials.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Credit Risk Management Guidelines: Training and Assessment Test for Approving Executives
programs.why: The CRM guidelines set minimum standards for staff who hold delegated approval powers: credit experience, training in financial statement, cash flow and risk analysis, and a pass in an assessment test covering credit analysis and loan management. Banks therefore need a structured credit risk course and test before granting approval authority.

references.title: Guidelines on Credit Risk Management (CRM) for Banks (BRPD Circular No. 04, 2016)
references.note: Executives with delegated loan approval powers must have set experience, training in financial statement, cash flow and risk analysis, and must pass an assessment test on credit analysis, structuring, documentation and loan management.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Treasury Dealing and Foreign Exchange Risk Management (FX Risk Guideline 2024)
programs.why: The revised FX risk guideline lets only trained staff work in treasury, requires banks to train treasury personnel, bars FX dealing with fewer than two trained and authorised dealers, and asks management to keep assessing dealers' training needs. It also covers dealing limits, mandatory leave and the dealer code of conduct.

references.title: Foreign Exchange Risk Management Guideline, December 2024
references.note: Only trained staff may work in treasury, banks must provide the required training to treasury personnel, dealing must not start with fewer than two trained and authorised dealers, and management must keep identifying dealers' training needs.

references.title: FE Circular Letter No. 12: Updating of Foreign Exchange Risk Management Guidelines
references.note: Replaces the 2016 foreign exchange risk guideline (BRPD Circular 01/2016) with the revised guideline and tells authorised dealers to comply at once.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Liquidity Risk, ALM and Basel III LCR/NSFR (Bangladesh Bank)
programs.why: The ALM guidelines require an ALCO, liquidity limits and Basel III liquidity ratios, and say liquidity is managed by officers with specialised knowledge. Bangladesh Bank revised NSFR reporting in July 2026. No separate course is prescribed, but ALM and treasury staff must be competent in these rules.

references.title: Asset-Liability Management (ALM) Guidelines (BRPD Circular No. 02, 2016)
references.note: Sets ALCO structure, Basel III liquidity ratios and liquidity management; officers responsible for liquidity must have specialised expertise and understand the bank's liquidity risk.

references.title: SDAD Circular Letter No. 11: Implementation of Basel III Liquidity Ratio
references.note: Keeps LCR and NSFR under DOS Circular 01/2015 and revises the NSFR reporting items so central bank repo and standing lending are reported as collateralised borrowing.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (Bangladesh Bank Guidelines)
programs.why: The IRRBB guidelines expect the board to understand the bank's interest rate risk strategy, some directors to be able to challenge IRRBB reports, and senior management to have the skills to measure and manage it. This is a competence duty without a set course.

references.title: Guidelines on Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book
references.note: The board must understand the bank's IRRBB strategy, some members must be able to challenge IRRBB reports, and the board must ensure senior management has the skills to manage IRRBB; ALCO may run the policy.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Basel III Risk Based Capital Adequacy (RBCA Guidelines)
programs.why: Banks calculate and report capital, buffers and the leverage ratio under Bangladesh Bank's Basel III RBCA guidelines. Staff preparing these returns and managing risk-weighted assets need working knowledge of the rules, though no specific training duty is set.

references.title: Guidelines on Risk Based Capital Adequacy (Revised Regulatory Capital Framework in line with Basel III)
references.note: Sets the Basel III capital definitions, minimum ratios, conservation buffer, leverage ratio and risk-weighting rules that banks report against.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Stress Testing under the 2024 Bangladesh Bank Guidelines
programs.why: Since December 2024 banks must run quarterly stress tests under revised guidelines and report them to the Financial Stability Department. The guidelines require stress testing staff to be adequately skilled in risk, macroeconomics, accounting and regulation, which is a competence duty.

references.title: Revised Guidelines on Stress Testing (FSD Circular No. 01, 2024)
references.note: Banks must run stress tests at least quarterly and report to the Financial Stability Department; stress testing staff must be adequately skilled in risk management, macroeconomics, accounting and the regulations.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Country Risk Management (Bangladesh Bank Guidelines 2021)
audience: International division and trade finance staff
programs.why: Banks with cross-border exposures must apply board-approved country risk policies, ratings, limits and monitoring. Staff handling correspondent, trade and treasury exposures need to understand these rules, though no course is prescribed.

references.title: Guidelines of Country Risk Management (BRPD Circular No. 07, 2021)
references.note: Requires banks with cross-border exposures to have board-approved country risk policies, country ratings, exposure limits, monitoring and provisioning.

programs.title: Bangladesh | ICT Outsourcing and Service Provider Management
programs.why: Banks must have a board-approved outsourcing policy, written contracts setting roles and obligations, evaluation of providers and contingency plans for critical outsourced services. Vendors should receive security awareness under the 2026 Cybersecurity Framework. These are framework duties rather than a staff training requirement.

references.title: Guideline on ICT Security for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions, Version 4.0 (issued by BRPD Circular No. 10 of 19 June 2023)
references.note: Requires a board-approved outsourcing policy, written agreements, risk-based evaluation of outsourcing, no weakening of internal controls, provider DR frameworks and contingency plans.

references.title: Guidelines on Cybersecurity Framework, Version 1.0 (2026)
references.note: Third-party vendors should receive awareness or training on their security roles and responsibilities.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (ICT Security Guideline v4.0)
programs.why: Banks must have a business continuity plan with a disaster recovery plan and site, and must test and exercise the plan with documented results, including cyber scenarios. Staff with BCP roles need to be ready through these exercises; no general training course is prescribed.

references.title: Guideline on ICT Security for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions, Version 4.0 (issued by BRPD Circular No. 10 of 19 June 2023)
references.note: Business continuity plans must be tested and exercised against defined scenarios, including cyber scenarios, with results and lessons recorded; a DRP and disaster recovery site are required.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Recovery Plans and the Bank Resolution Act 2026
programs.why: Banks must keep a board-approved recovery plan and update it every year, and the Bank Resolution Act 2026 gives Bangladesh Bank powers to resolve failing banks, linked to those plans. Bangladesh Bank placed five banks under resolution in November 2025. Senior staff need to understand both, though no training duty is set.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 03: Recovery Plan for Banks
references.note: Each bank must keep a board-approved recovery plan following the attached guidance, submit it to the Department of Off-site Supervision and update it by 31 January every year.

references.title: Bank Resolution Act, 2026 (Act No. 88 of 2026)
references.note: Gives Bangladesh Bank resolution powers over scheduled banks, links resolution to banks' recovery plans, and provides for resolution plans, temporary administration, bridge banks and bail-in. Act No. 108 of 2026 later removed section 18A.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Loan Write-off Policy and Written-off Loan Recovery Units
audience: Recovery and special asset management staff
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's write-off policy sets which classified loans may be written off, requires a dedicated recovery unit and, since November 2025, at least 10 working days' notice to the borrower. Recovery staff must apply these rules, though no course is prescribed.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 09: Policy on Loan/Investment Write-off and the Written-off Loan Recovery Unit
references.note: Bangla text. Amends the 2024 write-off policy: bad/loss loans with weak recovery prospects may be written off, oldest first, and the borrower must get at least 10 working days' notice before write-off.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Loan Rescheduling and Restructuring (BRPD Master Circular 16/2022)
programs.why: The rescheduling master circular sets minimum standards that each bank's own board-approved policy must follow, and 2025 policy support lets viable borrowers harmed before August 2024 restructure under set conditions. Credit staff must know these rules, though no training duty is stated.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 16: Master Circular on Loan Rescheduling and Restructuring
references.note: Bangla text. Sets the minimum standards for rescheduling and restructuring loans; each bank must adopt its own board-approved policy consistent with it.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 07: Policy support for restructuring the business and financial condition of the affected borrowers
references.note: Bangla text. Offers policy support to viable borrowers whose business was harmed by events before August 2024, with eligibility criteria and a set restructuring process.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Loan Classification and Provisioning (BRPD Master Circular 15/2024)
programs.why: Since April 2025 loans are classified by overdue period under a stricter master circular, with set provisions and revised CL reporting through the core banking system, as a bridge to IFRS 9 ECL. Credit and finance staff need sound knowledge of these rules, though no training duty is set.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 15: Master Circular on Loan Classification and Provisioning
references.note: Groups loans into four types and classifies them by overdue period (SMA from 2 months, substandard from 3 months) with set provisions, as a step toward ECL under IFRS 9; in force from 1 April 2025.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 05: Loan Classification and Provisioning (reporting)
references.note: Introduces revised CL-1 to CL-5 reporting forms generated through the core banking system from the September 2025 quarter and clarifies overdue rules for fixed term loans.

references.title: BRPD Circular Letter No. 29: Loan Classification and Provisioning
references.note: Sets a 0.5% provision on unclassified short-term agricultural credit and cottage, micro and small enterprise loans until 31 December 2026, replacing Circular Letter 22/2025.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Credit Information Bureau (CIB) Reporting
programs.why: Banks must upload every loan and credit card with any outstanding balance to Bangladesh Bank's CIB Online System by the 20th of each following month, and overdue credit cards must also be reported. Accurate reporting needs trained staff, though no training duty is set.

references.title: CIB Circular No. 01/2018: Resetting the threshold of submission of Credit Information to the CIB Database
references.note: All loans and credit cards with an outstanding balance of Tk 1 or more must be uploaded to the CIB Online System every month by the 20th of the following month.

programs.title: Bangladesh | CMSME Financing Master Circular: Half-Yearly Officer Training
programs.why: The 2025 CMSME master circular requires banks to train officers at branches, sub-branches and agent outlets through workshops or seminars held half-yearly or as needed, covering Bangladesh Bank's CMSME policy and run under the SME division. It also sets women entrepreneur and refinance rules these officers apply.

references.title: SMESPD Circular No. 01: Master Circular on CMSME Financing
references.note: Bangla text. Each bank must staff CMSME lending adequately and train officers at branches, sub-branches and agent outlets through half-yearly (or as needed) workshops or seminars that cover Bangladesh Bank's CMSME policy, under its SME division.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Agricultural and Rural Credit Policy FY 2026-27: Officer Awareness and Training
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's yearly agricultural credit policy applies to all scheduled banks, including private and foreign banks, and requires them to raise officers' awareness of the policy through training and workshops. Officers handling agri and rural credit therefore need policy training each cycle.

references.title: ACD-1 Circular No. 03: Agricultural and Rural Credit Policy and Program for FY 2026-2027
references.note: Bangla text. Banks must raise awareness of the agricultural credit policy among officers at all levels, including field level, through training and workshops, with support from Bangladesh Bank's Agricultural Credit Department-1.

references.title: BRPD Circular Letter No. 29: Loan Classification and Provisioning
references.note: Sets a 0.5% provision on unclassified short-term agricultural credit and cottage, micro and small enterprise loans until 31 December 2026, replacing Circular Letter 22/2025.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Genuine Banknote Identification in the Annual Training Programme
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's currency department told every scheduled bank to include identification of genuine banknotes and their security features in its annual training programme. Bank officials also provide note-checking services at seasonal markets and during Ramadan to curb counterfeit notes.

references.title: DCM Circular Letter No. 08/2016: Inclusion of identification of genuine bank notes in banks' annual training program
references.note: Bangla text. Banks must add a session on recognising genuine banknotes and their security features to their annual staff training programme and inform the Department of Currency Management.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Dormant Accounts and Unclaimed Deposits (Bank Company Act s.35)
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank sets when accounts become inoperative and dormant, requires notice before marking them, bans reactivation fees, and requires fresh KYC after 5 years. Deposits untouched for 10 years must be noticed and transferred to Bangladesh Bank. Branch staff must apply these steps, though no course is prescribed.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 23: Policy regarding the operation of Dormant Account
references.note: Bangla text. Accounts with no customer transaction for 6 months become inoperative and then dormant after a further 6 months (current, SND) or 18 months (savings); interest must still be paid, customers get a month's notice, reactivation is free, and fresh KYC is needed after 5 years.

references.title: BRPD Circular No. 10: Policy on Unclaimed Deposits & Valuables
references.note: Bangla text. Under section 35 of the Bank Company Act, deposits and valuables untouched for 10 years need a 3-month registered notice, an annual return to BRPD within 30 days of year end, and transfer to Bangladesh Bank each April.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2024
programs.why: The 2024 Act puts payment systems on a statutory footing, covering licensing, agents, outsourcing, confidentiality, unauthorised payments, cheques, interbank transfers and e-money. Payment staff need to know it, though it sets no training duty.

references.title: Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024 (Act No. 9 of 2024)
references.note: Requires Bangladesh Bank licensing of payment systems and services and covers outsourcing, agents, record keeping, confidentiality, unauthorised payment orders, cheques, interbank EFT and e-money.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Credit Card Operations Guidelines 2026
programs.why: The March 2026 credit card guidelines require card issuers to have enough properly trained staff to run card systems and to train employees on the card ICT policy and security. They also set rules on eligibility, consent, disclosure, harassment-free recovery and CIB reporting that card staff must follow.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 09: Guidelines on Credit Card Operations of Banks
references.note: Card issuers must have enough properly trained and competent staff to run card systems, must train employees on the card ICT policy, security and technology operations, and must follow fair marketing, consent and recovery rules.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Mobile Financial Services Regulations 2022: Staff and Agent Awareness
programs.why: MFS in Bangladesh is run through bank or FI subsidiaries. The 2022 regulations require MFS providers to run continuing awareness and knowledge programmes for employees, agents and distributors to improve financial literacy and fight fraud.

references.title: Bangladesh Mobile Financial Services (MFS) Regulations, 2022
references.note: MFS providers, which are bank or FI subsidiaries, must run continuing awareness and knowledge programmes on MFS for their employees, agents, distributors and target customers to build literacy and fight fraud.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Agent Banking: Training for Agents and Bank Officials
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank's agent banking guidelines require banks to train agents before and during operations, run regular training for agents and the bank officials linked to them, and keep an agent training manual. Training must cover customer identification, service, confidentiality, cash security and record keeping.

references.title: Prudential Guidelines for Agent Banking Operation in Bangladesh (BRPD Circular No. 14, 2017)
references.note: Banks must run regular training for agents and the bank officials who oversee them, train agents before and during operations on customer identification, service, confidentiality, cash security and record keeping, and keep an agent training manual.

references.title: BRPD Circular Letter No. 11: Prudential Guidelines for Agent Banking Operation in Bangladesh
references.note: Bangla cover letter with English text. Replaces paragraphs 24.5, 31.4, 35, 38.5.1 and 45.1 on two-factor authentication, quarterly or monthly outlet visits by bank staff, outlet relocation and quarterly reporting.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Foreign Exchange Regulations for Authorised Dealer Branches (FER Act and GFET)
programs.why: Banks deal in foreign exchange only through licensed AD branches under the FER Act 1947 and the GFET. To license a branch a bank must certify it has enough skilled and experienced FX officers. This is a competence requirement rather than a set course.

references.title: FEPD-2 Circular No. 07: Consolidated Circular - Licenses for Authorized Dealers, Money Changers and Gold Dealers
references.note: To license a branch as an authorised dealer, a bank must declare compliance with the FX risk guideline and certify that the branch has enough skilled and experienced officers for foreign exchange work.

references.title: Guidelines for Foreign Exchange Transactions (GFET), 2018 Vol 1
references.note: Bangladesh Bank's main rulebook for authorised dealers on FX accounts, remittances, imports, exports, LCs, travel and non-resident accounts; Chapter 2 expects AD banks to show adequate manpower trained in foreign exchange.

references.title: The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 (Act No. VII of 1947)
references.note: Parent law for authorised dealers and restrictions on foreign exchange dealings, payments and currency movements; Bangladesh Bank issues FX circulars under it.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Preventing Workplace Violence and Harassment (Labour Act s.332 as amended 2026)
programs.why: The Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act 2026 replaced section 332 of the Labour Act. Employers must prevent violence and harassment, adopt and apply a workplace policy, assess these risks and give workers information and training on the risks, the prevention measures and their rights and duties. A new section 332A requires a complaints committee. Banks are commercial establishments under the Act.

references.title: Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 43 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.provision: Section 82 (new section 332 of the Labour Act) and section 83 (new section 332A)
references.note: Employers must prevent violence and harassment, publicise the prohibitions and penalties, adopt a workplace policy, assess risks, train workers on risks, protections, rights and duties, and form a five-member complaints committee led by a woman.

references.title: Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 (Act No. 42 of 2006)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Banks and banking companies are listed as commercial establishments, so the Act's workplace duties reach bank employers.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Sexual Harassment Prevention at Work (Labour Act 2026 Amendments)
programs.why: The 2026 amendments add a statutory definition of sexual harassment to the Labour Act and require employers to publicise the prohibitions and penalties, take effective preventive measures, and provide training on harassment risks and protections. Bangladesh Bank's Code of Conduct separately bans harassment by directors and staff.

references.title: Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 43 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.provision: Section 4 (new definition in section 2(52A)) and section 82 (new section 332)
references.note: Defines sexual harassment and requires employers to publicise penalties, prevent harassment, provide information and training, publish complaint procedures and support legal action.

references.title: Code of Conduct for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions
references.note: Banks must keep the workplace free of harassment, including sexual harassment of women, and must not tolerate harassment by directors, managers or staff.

programs.title: Bangladesh | IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss Implementation (Bangladesh Bank Roadmap)
programs.why: Bangladesh Bank requires banks to train all relevant officials on ECL-based classification and provisioning, run regular IFRS 9 training and train-the-trainer programmes, and ensure ECL work is done by well-trained staff. ECL under IFRS 9 applies to credit facilities by January 2028.

references.title: BRPD Circular Letter No. 03: Implementation of ECL-based Loan Classification and Provisioning under IFRS 9
references.note: Sets the IFRS 9 roadmap: banks must form an implementation team including the CRO and CFO, train all relevant employees on ECL-based classification (deadline January 2026), run regular training, and arrange train-the-trainer programmes for their training institutes.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 06: Guidance for banks in implementing IFRS 9 Financial Instruments
references.note: Minimum IFRS 9 requirements: senior management must have ECL estimated by well-trained staff and train those involved in ECL models; risk staff need regular training. Applies to credit facilities by January 2028 and other instruments by January 2029.

programs.title: Bangladesh | Electronic KYC (e-KYC) Guidelines 2026
programs.why: From 1 September 2026, banks onboarding customers remotely must follow Bangladesh Bank's e-KYC guidelines, using NID and biometrics with simplified or regular e-KYC and digital risk grading, and report implementation quarterly. Staff need to know these steps; the AML training duty is covered under program 4.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 08: Guidelines on Electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC)
references.note: Issues updated e-KYC guidelines for banks, finance companies and payment providers, replacing BFIU Circular 25 (2020) from 1 September 2026, with quarterly implementation reporting.

references.title: Guidelines on Electronic Know-Your-Customer (e-KYC), March 2026
references.note: NID and biometric-based remote onboarding with simplified e-KYC for proven low-risk, limited-transaction accounts and regular or enhanced e-KYC with digital risk grading for others.

notes: The 2024-2025 interim government governed by ordinances. Parliament elected in February 2026 replaced most of them with Acts passed on 10 April 2026: the Personal Data Protection Act, Cyber Security Act (amended again by Act 99 of 2026 on 1 July 2026), Deposit Protection Act, Bank Resolution Act, Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Act and Labour (Amendment) Act. The ordinances are marked repealed on the Laws of Bangladesh portal.

Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Act 2026 (Act 28, 10 April 2026) amends sections 18 and 20 on measures against entities and repeals the Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Ordinance 2025; acts done under the ordinance remain valid.

Personal Data Protection Act 2026 (Act 63) is deemed in force from 6 November 2025, but section 23 (Chief Data Officer) and sections 31-35 (complaints, fines, compensation) start on a date to be notified after 18 months. It works alongside the National Data Management Act 2026.

Bangladesh Bank's Guidelines on Internal Control Management System (BRPD-2 Circular 03, 21 July 2026) replaced the 2016 ICC guidelines (BRPD Circulars 03/2016 and 06/2016). Banks must restructure by 31 December 2026.
Bangladesh Bank Cybersecurity Framework v1.0 was issued by BRPD-2 Circular 02 on 29 March 2026, with compliance due by 31 December 2026. It sits alongside the ICT Security Guideline v4.0 (2023).

BRPD-1 Circular 10 (7 May 2026) made foundation training of at least 14 weeks mandatory for confirming newly recruited scheduled bank officers. Bangladesh Bank also issued new e-KYC guidelines in March 2026.

The Bank Company (Amendment) Act 2023 (Act 13, 26 June 2023) reshaped board composition and independent director rules. BRPD Circular 02/2024, with later circular letters (Dec 2024, Aug 2025), sets board duties and director fitness rules.

BFIU Circular 26 (2020) is still the master AML circular for scheduled banks; BFIU issued new sector circulars (Nos. 30-34) for other sectors in 2026. The 2015 ML/TF risk management guidelines still refer to the older Circular 10, so read them alongside Circular 26. BFIU's February 2026 transaction monitoring circular letter is published only as a scanned image.

Deposit Protection Act 2026 replaced the Bank Deposit Insurance Act 2000. The Consumer Rights Protection Act 2009 does not list banking among the services it covers, so bank customer protection rests on Bangladesh Bank guidelines.

Breadth review (November 2026): loan classification moved to overdue-based rules under BRPD Circular 15/2024 from 1 April 2025, and IFRS 9 ECL applies to credit facilities by January 2028 (other instruments January 2029). Bangladesh Bank also issued credit card guidelines (March 2026), e-KYC guidelines in force from 1 September 2026, and a consolidated AD licence circular (October 2026). Act 108 of 2026 amended the Bank Resolution Act 2026.
